doc.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: More on Elvis: concerts, dates and farewell
summary: Nice guy, sad death; the major jobs were Madison Square Garden and Honolulu.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Plus he was a nice guy. He seemed like a real nice guy and it was a very sad thing when he died. I felt sort of bad about that.
Were you on the band when, I’m not sure if it was the Hawaii concert or, I guess it was in Las Vegas, where he actually sat at the piano and played?
I never knew he did that until I saw that.

That would have been Las Vegas I feel. I did tours with him twice. But the two biggest jobs were the recordings that we did were “Live at Madison Square Garden” and what was it, Elvis in Honolulu? I forgot the title of that particular album that we did but it was the first Telstar show that was ever filmed, that was ever beamed down to—
A broadcast. That was it. And then I never went with him again, that was it.
I don’t know, it’s on that paper. I can’t recollect when it was. I don’t know, it was in the ‘70s wasn’t it somewhere? It would be interesting if you could tell me.
Yeah it must have been in the 70s. Okay. After leaving Les Brown he was with Elvis. Probably early 70s.
Yeah. I would have to say it was around there.
Interesting. Well it’s great to hear that you’ve had not only the jazz thing but a little bit of country, and little bit of Elvis. You got any other curve balls to throw at me here?
